parsed.explanation: Combined regime is elevated risk: federal entry screening can refuse on document discrepancy and pursue lifetime fraud ineligibility, federal facilities require birth sex, and documented national/immigration custody abuse follows detention. The state layer mitigates: no current facility ban or criminalisation, repealed 2016 law, local protections for ~30% population. But no statewide private-sector/hate-crime recourse, 2025 revived bathroom bill, minors' care and sports bans, and amended certificates retaining original sex keep exposure universal at borders/federal sites. No execution or likely imprisonment for presence alone; functioning courts provide partial, unresolved remedies.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary-sex order; X/new mismatched passports stopped Feb 2025, Supreme Court Nov 2025 allowed it. Entry cable: document discrepancy causing reasonable doubt requires refusal and more evidence; suspected wilful misrepresentation may support permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility (four elements, not automatic).
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid to expiry; ACLU suit for seven plaintiffs and other litigation unresolved; several 2025 orders enjoined.
entry_documents.interaction: Discrepancy at entry can escalate to investigation, refusal, or fraud allegation, then detention/custody exposures.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: From 2026 national corrections bureau adopted model described as conversion therapy: short hair, hormone removal, psychiatric drugs; immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Courts challenge orders; no documented effective remedy for custody practices in dossier.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Immigration or criminal detention triggers birth-sex placement, care denial and abuse risk; state also bars public funds for transition care in prison.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars use of government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. State has no current facility ban/criminalisation after 2017 repeal, but 2025 legislature revived bathroom bill; status uncertain.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State repeal in 2017; no state statute bars facility matching identity; local ordinances in largest city and one county from 2022.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal buildings/airports apply birth-sex rule even where state/local facilities do not; revived state bill could close state gap.

care_services.exposure: State laws effective Aug 2023 end puberty blockers, hormone therapy and surgery under 18; 2025 law bars state funds for minors and prisoners. National orders target minors' care and some are litigated.
care_services.protection: No documented visitor protection for non-emergency gender care; adult routine care not documented as barred.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor needing continuity faces state ban regardless of home treatment; detained adult faces hormone removal under national model.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders redefine sex as binary, remove gender-identity materials/policies, prosecute teachers facilitating social transition, sports/entry bans. May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises groups described as radically pro-transgender, while stating mere disagreement is not targeted.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Several orders blocked/enjoined; national employment and hate-crime statutes exist, but state hate-crime law covers neither gender identity nor sexual orientation.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing raises police/administrative discretion at borders and schools, though reward memo never uses radical gender ideology as criterion.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minor visitor subject to state care ban and ban on assigned-male-at-birth participation in female sports; school parents-rights law requires notification on name/pronoun requests for residents and bars K-4 instruction.
minors_guardians.protection: No documented visitor-specific guardian protection; parents' rights and local school policies vary.
minors_guardians.interaction: Guardian travelling with minor cannot obtain state-funded transition care or female-team sports entry; care-seeking can expose family to records/investigation context nationally.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No statewide private employment/housing/public-accommodations protection; only ~30% population under local gender-identity ordinances. State bias-crime law excludes gender identity, limiting bias charging/recourse. 2025 poll: 66% support assigned-sex document laws.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 22 states plus capital district outlaw gender-identity discrimination, not this state statewide.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Assault may be prosecuted generally but not as state bias crime; remedy depends on city/county ordinance and local police.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport, executive-order and health-rule litigation unresolved; travel exposure depends on measures in force at travel. Outcome of 2025 bathroom bill, county application of amended-certificate original-sex display, and local enforcement not established.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ, civil-liberties litigation, courts enjoining some orders, and local ordinances provide partial recourse.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies may operate after refusal/detention but cannot reliably prevent initial outing, refusal, or custody placement.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar universal border exclusion without guaranteed imprisonment and weak appeal, but here refusal is discretionary, fraud requires four elements, and courts actively litigate; lower than 0.35 would require routine exclusion as settled practice.

Higher than this case: 0.55 is mainly delay, secondary screening and administrative denial. Here federal facility ban, possible lifetime ineligibility, and documented severe custody abuse push materially below 0.55.

Lower than 0.75: there, mismatched documents cause brief detention with counsel/compensation and working tribunal. Here entry refusal/fraud, federal facility exclusion, custody harm, and no statewide bias recourse lack such operative protection.

parsed.synthesis: The operative interaction is federal-first: document/presentation mismatch at entry or in a federal facility triggers birth-sex treatment, possible refusal/fraud pursuit, and if detained, documented care denial and abuse. The state layer softens street/facility risk—no current ban, repealed 2016 law, some local ordinances—but adds minors' care/sports bans, certificate disclosure, and no statewide anti-discrimination or bias-crime recourse. Courts and litigation moderate, not eliminate, exposure. Hence elevated risk, above organised-targeting and imprisonment regimes, below administrative-friction regimes.
